name: Can commercial project management reduce change orders?

mainEntity.name: Can hiring a project manager reduce change orders on a commercial project?
mainEntity.text: Can hiring a project manager reduce change orders on a commercial project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change orders often happen when scope is vague, drawings are incomplete, or field conditions differ from assumptions. A commercial project manager helps reduce those problems by tightening scope definition early, coordinating design reviews, comparing bids carefully, and tracking decisions before procurement begins. They also make sure owner requests are priced and approved before the work proceeds, which prevents unauthorized extras from piling up. While no project can eliminate change orders entirely, good management can reduce the number, size, and timing of them. This matters because change orders usually affect both budget and schedule. Owners should ask how the manager handles scope validation, contingency use, and approval workflows. A disciplined process does not remove all risk, but it makes the project much more predictable.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A strong project manager can reduce change orders by defining scope clearly, reviewing plans early, coordinating pricing before work starts, and catching conflicts before construction begins. Fewer surprises during the build usually means fewer cost increases later.
